I engaged Shure and Lucia in a discussion while walking, confirming that potatoes qualify as a staple food due to their starch content and considering breakfast options such as mashed potatoes and bread. The group debated whether to order food or have a BBQ, ultimately concluding the discussion as we continued walking together.

Katrina raised the need for more fruit, suggesting easy-to-peel types. I inquired about the specific fruit she had in mind. Tasha expressed reluctance to have assistance cutting fruit; I examined a square melon and nearby mangosteen. After discussing prices, I chose to buy a mangosteen based on Tasha’s advice and fruit size. Holding the mangosteen, I walked with Tasha as she confirmed no additional fruits beyond our selected seven and speculated others had gone for drinks.

Near the freezer, I discussed durian options with Tasha, mentioning “durian pizza” and considering buying durian priced at 98. Tasha pointed out a smaller durian, and Shure reminded us to get cooking wine. I followed Tasha to inspect the smaller durian, then approached the shelf and agreed to buy two boxes of durian pizza for lunch, with Tasha retrieving them. We confirmed the purchase before moving on.

While walking, I asked Tasha about her sweet drink; after she showed me a juice bottle, we decided that one small bottle was sufficient, avoiding the larger size. Later, I clarified a previous shopping intent from "king crab" to "oil" with Violet and Tasha, noting corn oil might be inadequate. We proceeded to the seafood restaurant, passing the seafood tank, where I pointed out the seafood section and apologized to Tasha for bumping into her.

At the seafood area, I recounted a past Singapore visit involving big crab with Violet and discussed dining costs at Xinli. Joining a group by the seafood tank, I engaged in price discussions of king crab and Boston lobster with Lucia, comparing local and foreign prices while observing seafood and tags.

I coordinated a group shopping trip for ingredients, standing with Lucia and others around the cart. I placed the mangosteen inside as Alice organized items. Shure inquired about fennel and cumin; we confirmed cumin was still needed. I proposed preparing breakfast the next morning, leading the group to plan the meal and confirm purchases of bread, ketchup, and lettuce for sandwiches. Alice noted bread was not yet bought; we agreed to toast it.

The group discussed next-day logistics including package deliveries and staying indoors. I interacted with Violet and others about plans and job details related to Lucia. After Tasha and Shure said goodbye to Violet, I confirmed attendance for an upcoming meeting with six participants. I took an item from Violet and used WeChat on my phone to coordinate with the group.

We clarified spice details, distinguishing cumin seeds and powder, and checked ingredients like white pepper and chili flakes. Bread purchase status was revisited; Alice confirmed it was still needed. We collectively decided to buy bread and ketchup. I continued managing communications while the group prepared to move on. Lucia mentioned a missing item, and Katrina reminded us it was mealtime as we proceeded shopping.

As the group moved through the market, I initiated interaction by pointing out wontons and discussing clam purchases with Alice and Shure. I used my phone to message via WeChat, inquired about tasting cups, gathered pricing, and sampled food while noting product brands. I observed Tasha working on her phone in the dairy section, capturing the methodical exploration and decision-making during our shopping.

I approached Tasha, Lucia, and Alice near the cart discussing tomato boxes and portions. I opened WeChat while listening to their plan to distribute 200 grams per person starting with three cups. Tasha mentioned joining my yogurt group; we debated yogurt quantity and taste. I sampled yogurt and discussed a drink called Douzhi with Tasha, examining price and replenishment needs.

I inspected a bag Lucia placed in the cart and handed it to Shure. We compared item prices to Singapore, expressing surprise. I clarified total spending and shared light moments with the group. When Katrina asked about bread with tomato sauce, I examined the bottle then followed the group to a shelf for item selection.

At the shelf, Katrina asked about cheese and jam; Shure mentioned leftover garlic. Katrina proposed buying two bags of cheese for six people, which I agreed to. Shure noted no spicy garlic remained; Katrina asked what to get with the two bags. The group coordinated supplies and quantities accordingly.

While walking with Tasha, Alice, Katrina, Shure, and Lucia, I searched multiple shelves for ketchup per Katrina’s request. Alice and Katrina discussed British lunch customs, and Shure noted the need for more ketchup and home oil availability. We moved between the yogurt section and other aisles as I monitored time and messages, confirming roughly 40 minutes remained for our task.

The group conversed about items like king crab legs and refrigerated products. Katrina confirmed if oil was needed. Shure decided the car could not fit all items, leading to purchase limitations. We stood discussing progress, with Shure commenting on expenses and Alice noting item counts. I checked yogurt sections and adjusted my hat, concluding by assessing the situation.

I held a hat while moving forward and observing the group. Shure found an item; I suggested proceeding and checked if anyone was missing. Tasha explained visibility challenges and discussed item weights and prices, after which she put an item back. I proceeded to another shelf where Katrina inquired about membership benefits; Shure suggested eggs. I entered the free vegetable section, observing the group.

Shure called my name; I logged out of WeChat on my phone. Alice noted an incorrect home address; I inquired about verification codes. Shure explained they used the Hema app; I input the code and reopened it. Everyone checked their phones; Alice considered turning off the app but Shure reminded us of payment. I entered payment details, signaled readiness, and approved scanning the next item.

Near checkout, I observed Tasha operating the scanner and discussing coupon usage with Alice, who asked about more coupons; I declined. Katrina asked about membership benefits. I approached Lucia, joked about a one-star coin coupon, and mentioned connection issues. Tasha and Shure encouraged me to attempt a purchase; I complied while Katrina and Tasha scanned codes. I adjusted my glasses, organized hats beside the cart, and observed the group finishing scanning.

At the checkout packing area, I put on my hat, adjusted glasses, and held the cart while observing Katrina scanning and Shure bagging items. I assisted Alice bagging food and asked about a bag she used, learning it was purchased. We discussed bag expenses as I held one. Alice requested passing seasoning; I continued holding the bag while items were organized.

Tasha joined standing to my left. The group discussed using a discount card purchased earlier for an 8% savings versus opening a new one. Lucia placed fruit into the bag I held. I considered opening the card and discussed costs with Tasha. We chatted while tidying groceries, with Shure prompting to proceed and Lucia directing item placement. The group managed checkout and packing efficiently, focusing on cost savings.

After shopping, I inspected the car and bags, pointed out items, and directed attention to the cart and receipt held by Tasha. Tasha, Alice, Lucia, and Shure handled packing fragile items like eggs and drinks, discussing protection strategies. I assigned "egg protector" roles and oversaw packing. The group debated temporary item placement and managing the cart. After finalizing loading, I pushed the cart out, noting missing Pepsi and briefly discussing beverage preferences. Attempts to maneuver the cart failed, and the empty cart was taken by staff.

Carrying eggs and other items upstairs via escalator, the group arranged protective strategies. Shure proposed guarding eggs individually, which I accepted despite concerns about personnel. We exchanged remarks on egg care while ascending. During the ride, the group conversed about mental states. Upon reaching the upper level, I led the group forward, signaling readiness to continue.

I walked upstairs with Tasha and Shure from the lower to the upper level, explaining the need to move upstairs. We passed doors and used the escalator. Tasha commented on the number of steps and my footwear comfort; I explained my Singapore slippers had thicker soles for easier walking. This completed our transition to the upper floor.

At the upper level, we encountered Lucia and Alice near a gashapon machine, briefly discussing its function and my slippers’ condition. I switched my bag and opened WeChat, consulting Shure about arranging a business ride for six people. We discussed waiting spots and photo opportunities at HeyTea. I checked an electronic map to identify pick-up locations. Shure and I analyzed and confirmed the current location as suitable.

The group exchanged brief comments on surroundings, including Alice and Lucia noting a hole resembling a creepy smile, which I dismissed by shrinking the map view. Preparations for departure were settled with agreement on the pick-up spot, concluding planning and positioning before arranging transportation.

I initiated ordering a taxi by selecting the destination and browsing car models on my phone, confirming the ride while monitoring the "matching in progress" status. Meanwhile, Shure, Alice, Tasha, and Lucia discussed perseverance and optimism, which I acknowledged but remained focused on my phone. We prepared to wait for the taxi, placing belongings on the ground as instructed by Shure, who also confirmed purchases with Alice. I used my phone’s camera to direct the group in recording videos, coordinating them to look up and smile to capture a collective moment. This established our readiness and documentation before departure.

Shure proposed activating an AI wake-up service, which I agreed to, introducing myself as Katrina. The group gathered around the phone for photos and videos, with Shure directing the sequence—first group photos, then videos. I ensured everyone, including Alice who was initially missing, was properly framed and retook photos as needed. We exchanged brief comments on appearances and camera settings to enhance coordination. After the session, I placed pocket items onto a hat during filming. Shure noted the year 2077, and I remembered an additional item. Light-hearted remarks about WiFi signal issues followed, concluding the documentation segment with the group in good spirits.

Post-recording, I adjusted my hat after Alice corrected its position, maintaining a preferred crooked look. We gathered for a group photo, with me pressing the shutter and stepping forward after. Shure complimented the photo, and I suggested reviewing videos sequentially, prompting Shure to begin promptly. As we prepared, Alice, Lucia, Tasha, Shure, and I greeted each other with “You’re awake,” shaking me playfully. I saved the photos, instructed the group to disperse, adjusted my hat, and checked photos on my phone.
